content.text:
In this dataset, "L groin trouble" is 0 for all 16,384 patients, so the data can't show a statistical link either way. I'm answering from the structure of the diagnosis instead.

The file's labels fall into pathophysiological diagnoses (such as radiculopathy and discoligamentous injury) and symptom diagnoses (such as groin trouble). In neuropathic pain diagnosis, the pathophysiological cause (nerve root damage) produces the symptom, not the reverse. A right L1 radiculopathy would therefore cause groin trouble, so B is more likely than A.

ANSWER: B
